edits.find: The biopsy result is a premise, not a puzzle — the stem names the lesion for you. The question is what membranous nephropathy means in a 17-year-old, and it turns on one epidemiological fact: membranous nephropathy in adults is usually primary; in children it is usually secondary. So the diagnosis obliges a search for a cause, and the highest-yield one is hepatitis B, where circulating HBeAg–anti-HBeAg immune complexes deposit subepithelially and produce exactly this picture. Evaluating all patients with membranous nephropathy for hepatitis B is recommended; in a child it is close to mandatory.
